practices.practice: Keep DocumentDB connection strings and DB credentials in environment variables or a managed secret store and never commit them to the repository or test fixtures.
practices.prior_belief: Store the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string and any DB credentials only in environment variables or a managed secret store (Azure Key Vault); never hard-code or commit them to the repository or test fixtures.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (managed identities) and RBAC for authentication so apps use short-lived credentials rather than long-lived DB passwords; if SCRAM is used, create per-app least-privilege users and rotate secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Retrieve DB credentials at runtime from Azure Key Vault (or another managed secret store) and grant the app principal least-privilege access to the secret instead of embedding passwords in CI or code.

practices.practice: Always require TLS for client connections and do not disable certificate validation in production; configure CA bundles correctly for development instead of turning off verification.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for connections (use the connection string option tls=true/ssl=true) and enforce certificate validation; ensure client drivers are configured to refuse insecure connections.

practices.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient/Async client at process startup and reuse it across requests rather than creating a new client per request or operation.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single shared Motor/MongoClient instance at application startup and reuse it for all operations; do not open a new client per request or per operation.

practices.practice: Tune driver connection-pool and timeout settings (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize/connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS) to match the workload, using small pools for serverless and larger pools for long-running servers.
practices.prior_belief: Tune the driver's connection pool settings (e.g., maxPoolSize/minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) appropriate to the workload and set them explicitly in the connection URI or client options.

practices.practice: Implement retry and exponential backoff (with jitter) for transient errors and rate-limited responses, detect 429s and retryable error codes, and respect any Retry-After guidance from the service.
practices.prior_belief: Implement robust retry/backoff logic for transient failures and rate-limited responses: detect HTTP 429 or the driver's equivalent, respect the Retry-After header, and use exponential backoff with jitter for retries.

practices.practice: Size cluster capacity by picking the appropriate compute tier and storage type (IOPS/bandwidth are gated by compute tier for Premium SSD v2) and use autoscale or larger tiers for heavy batch workloads rather than thinking in Cosmos DB RU/s.
practices.prior_belief: Provision collection throughput (RU/s) or autoscale appropriately for the de-identification pipeline's read/write pattern; benchmark and raise RUs or enable autoscale to avoid frequent throttling during batch runs.

practices.practice: Choose shard/partition keys to obtain even distribution: for read-heavy workloads pick the most-used query filter; for write-heavy workloads pick a high-cardinality, evenly distributed field and avoid monotonic keys.
practices.prior_belief: Design partition keys to evenly distribute data and avoid cross-partition hot spots — pick a high-cardinality field used in query filters (e.g., patientId or sourceId) rather than _id or a low-cardinality constant.

practices.practice: Create explicit indexes on fields your application queries frequently (for example sourceId and created_at) and use compound indexes when queries filter or sort on multiple fields.
practices.prior_belief: Create explicit indexes on all fields the app queries frequently (for example: sourceId, deid_status, createdAt); use compound indexes where queries filter multiple fields, and add unique indexes when you must prevent duplicates (e.g., unique index on DeidNote.sourceId).

practices.practice: Keep small indexed fields for status/processed checks (for example deid_status + sourceId) so efficient lookups support idempotent batch processing.
practices.prior_belief: For derived/documented status checks (hasBeenDeid, deidVersion, deidTimestamp) keep small indexed fields to allow efficient lookups for unprocessed notes and to support idempotent pipelines (e.g., index deid_status + sourceId).

practices.practice: Enforce schema and model validation at the application or DB layer (use Pydantic/Beanie model validation or MongoDB schema validation) and include a schemaVersion field to support migrations.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce schema/field constraints at the application or DB layer (Beanie model validation, Mongo schema validation) so RawNote always has the fields required for de-identification (sourceId/patientId, text, createdAt) and DeidNote always references sourceId and deid metadata.

practices.practice: Make the de-identification pipeline idempotent by ensuring exactly one DeidNote per RawNote, using a unique index on DeidNote.sourceId or an upsert/check pattern to avoid duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Make the de-identification pipeline idempotent: mark notes as processed, use a unique index on DeidNote.sourceId (or use findOneAndUpdate with upsert=false and a filter that checks a processed flag) so repeated runs don't create duplicates.

practices.practice: Avoid storing very large clinical blobs directly in documents; split large fields into a side collection or store attachments in Azure Blob Storage and reference them to stay well under the 16 MB BSON limit.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing large clinical blobs directly in documents; if notes or attachments can be very large, store them in Azure Blob Storage and reference them from the document to stay within document-size limits and reduce RU cost.

practices.practice: Do not log PHI or connection strings: redact or hash identifiers in application logs and use synthetic data for CI and local testing.
practices.prior_belief: Do not log PHI (raw text) or DB connection strings; redact or hash identifiers in application logs and ensure CI tests and local dry-runs use synthetic data only.

practices.practice: Before sending clinical text to an external LLM, verify compliance and minimize PHI exposure; there is no authoritative Azure DocumentDB public guidance that endorses sending PHI to external LLMs for de-identification.
practices.prior_belief: Before sending clinical text to external LLM services, verify compliance and minimize PHI exposure (use on-prem or contractual protections like a BAA); where possible, perform local regex/tokenization pre-filtering and only send minimal context needed for de-identification.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB documentation + installed skills searched for LLM or OpenAI PHI guidance; no authoritative guidance found

practices.practice: When using vector search, store fixed-length float arrays, set the index dimension equal to the vector length, choose similarity (COS/IP/L2), and pick DiskANN/HNSW/IVF with tuned build/search parameters and normalized embeddings for cosine similarity.
practices.prior_belief: When using vector search, store vectors as fixed-length float arrays and create a vector index configured for the use-case: set dimension to vector length, choose similarity (cosine/inner_product), and configure HNSW params (m, efConstruction) and runtime ef for latency/recall tradeoffs.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging and alert on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, and connection saturation (and frequent 429s); use Log Analytics for slow-query analysis rather than relying on RU metrics.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor query RU charge and latency (via driver command monitoring or Azure Monitor/Diagnostic settings); add alerts for sustained high RU consumption or frequent 429s and capture slow query patterns to optimize indexes/queries.

practices.practice: Create and change indexes in a controlled manner (during deployment or maintenance windows), use explicit create_indexes scripts, and prefer sparse/partial/TTL options to limit index write cost.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes in a controlled manner (during deployment or a maintenance window) and avoid unbounded automatic index creation in hot workloads; prefer explicit create_indexes calls in scripts so you can tune index options (sparse/partial, TTL for ephemeral docs).

practices.practice: When a workflow spans multiple documents or partitions, plan for at-least-once semantics and use idempotency keys or compensating actions because cross-partition transactions are supported but can be expensive.
practices.prior_belief: Handle partial failures and multi-document workflows carefully: use 'at-least-once' semantics with idempotency keys (sourceId + deidVersion) and compensating actions rather than assuming multi-document transactions will always be available or cheap across partitions.
practices.how_found: searched installed skills for 'idempotent', 'multi-document transactions' and 'compensating actions' in Azure DocumentDB guidance; found discussion that cross-shard transactions are supported but not explicit application-level guidance

practices.practice: Run automated tests against a dedicated test database or a local DocumentDB gateway/emulator, keep seed scripts idempotent, and avoid running tests that modify production collections.
practices.prior_belief: Run automated tests against a dedicated test database or a local emulator (if available) and ensure seed scripts are idempotent and cleaned up after tests; never run tests that modify production collections.

practices.practice: On Azure DocumentDB prefer the `textSearch` index and the `$search` aggregation stage for lexical full-text search rather than relying on the community `$text` index.
Prefer Premium SSD v2 for new clusters because it decouples IOPS/bandwidth from disk size and requires sizing compute for throughput while sizing storage for capacity.

For local development, use the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (Mongo protocol on port 10260) and drive TLS relaxation and connection URIs from environment variables rather than hard-coding relaxed TLS in code.
